findings.title: Stale Pre-Vote round survives leader establishment and makes the new Leader start a real election
findings.summary: With Pre-Vote enabled, the election timer of a node that is still a Candidate starts a Pre-Vote round for term T+1 while its term-T candidacy stays live (pre_elect does not end it; the tick skips only Leaders). If a delayed term-T grant then makes it Leader, establish_leader/become_leader leave Engine.pre_candidate in place. When the stale round's granted pre-vote responses reach quorum, handle_pre_vote_resp calls elect() on the established Leader: the vote becomes (T+1, self, uncommitted) and server_state Candidate while the term-T Engine.leader object remains, violating try_leader_handler's debug assertion leader.committed_vote >= state.vote (observed panicking on the real Engine in traces/candidate_pre_vote_then_leader.ndjson.observation.json) and disrupting a healthy, freshly elected leader, contrary to the Pre-Vote contract (pre_vote.md:3-5,14-20; trigger.rs:47-56). TLC found it with Pre-Vote always on, no administrative election, no crash and no message loss; the violation is also reached over the complete MCNext (spec/output/v1-mc-update-full-U4.log, 13 states) and its precursor (Leader holding a pre-candidate) in spec/output/v1-mc-update-full.log.
